title: Local hypercohomology in a proper/open boundary test
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and let p:B→D and r:C→E be proper, k:C→B and i:E→D quasi-compact open immersions with k≫p=r≫i. Let J be an injective constant-A module sheaf on C, and let w be the clopen factorization witness [lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic-geometry]. Let W be an affine pro-etale object over D whose evaluation on set sheaves sends epimorphisms to surjections, and all of whose points specialize into W times_D Z, with Z the reduced closed complement of i. For every natural q>0, the ordinary hypercohomology group H^q(B times_D W,k_!J[0]) vanishes. Here extension is [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and object hypercohomology is the K-injective section-complex construction [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] on the original constant ring coefficients [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. This is a local section group; it does not assert vanishing of a higher direct image or of its closed restriction.

proof.text: Pull back the proper/open square along the weakly etale affine test W. The proper/open hypotheses persist, and the clopen factor in the witness pulls back to a clopen open U inside P times_W E_W. Weakly etale restriction preserves injectivity of J. Open-extension base change identifies the restricted coefficient sheaf with k_W!J_W.

Compute cohomology using an injective resolution of k_W!J_W on P, not a resolution of J_W. Refine by the finite principal-open and complementary closed-localization cover. Properness makes the image of a closed support closed, so an open support cannot persist on a boundary-specializing piece. Use injectivity on the clopen part to lift positive cocycles with these zero boundary restrictions; compatible lifts glue after refinement. This is the inherited arbitrary-injective local boundary-cohomology calculation, whose Lean proof remains open. No etale-origin-only boundary statement is invoked.

proof_origin.description: Makes the indicated local step of the existing boundary-restriction plan explicit; the closed-restriction detection statement has a complete Lean proof.

mathlib_searches.query: Positive hypercohomology of the extension by zero of an injective pro-etale sheaf on a proper pullback over a weakly contractible affine boundary specialization neighborhood is zero
mathlib_searches.verdict: Only general injective-resolution declarations; no local proper/open vanishing theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: Positive hypercohomology of an injective sheaf extended by zero along an open in a proper morphism over a weakly contractible affine specializing to its closed complement
mathlib_searches.verdict: No match: open extension itself is not assumed injective.
No match. The project proper-boundary theorem has an additional etale-origin assumption, so it does not prove this statement.

theorem isZero_properOpen_boundary_test_hypercohomology
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {B D C E : Scheme.{u}} (p : B ⟶ D) (r : C ⟶ E)
    (k : C ⟶ B) (i : E ⟶ D)
    [IsProper p] [IsProper r]
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [QuasiCompact k]
    [IsOpenImmersion i] [QuasiCompact i]
    (hcomm : k ≫ p = r ≫ i)
    (J : proEtaleRingModules C (proEtaleConstantRing C A)) [Injective J]
    (w : OpenProperClopenWitness p r k i)
    (W : D.ProEt) [IsAffine W.left]
    (hW : ∀ (F G : Sheaf (ProEt.topology D) (Type (u + 1))) (e : F ⟶ G),
      Epi e → Function.Surjective (e.hom.app (op W)))
    (hspecializes : ∀ x : W.left, ∃ z : ↥(pullback W.hom i.closedComplement),
      Specializes x ((pullback.fst W.hom i.closedComplement) z))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero ((ProEt.ringHypercohomology B
      ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology B)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj
          (proEtaleConstantRing B A)) ((proEtaleBaseChange p).obj W) (q : ℤ)).obj
            ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
              (proEtaleRingModules B (proEtaleConstantRing B A)) 0).obj
                ((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero k A).obj J)))
